Strike, Heng Foong Silk Weaving Factory, 23 Haichow Road.

Sir,

Further to strike report Misc. No. 116/41, enquiries
at the Heng Foong ( 恒丰 ) Silk Weaving Factory have
now ascertained that all strikers unconditionally return-
ed to work on the 14/10/41, the management having refused
to grant an increase in wages.

Owing to the management engaging new employees, the
strikers became alarmed and thus returned to work.

The management has promised to immediately inform
the undersigned should there be any further signs of
unrest.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Subject Further report on strike at Hung Foong Silk Filature,
23 Haichow Road.
Made by D.S.I. Kennedy Forwarded by B. Palmer Supt.

Sir,

The undersigned, D. S. I. Sung Ah Poh and C.D.C. 108 proceeded to the Hung Foong Silk Filature, 23 Haichow Road on the afternoon of 1/3/39 when the following arrangements were made. Property consisting of bed clothing etc belonging to the strikers who refused to go back to work, after negotiations between them and the Management, was removed to the factory, where it could subsequently be collected by the men concerned. The Management posted two Indian watchmen outside the Filature Quarters with instructions to keep out any of the former employees who refuse to work and consequently have no right to occupy the premises. On 1/3/39 thirty of the strikers resumed work, making a total of 47 males employed out of the usual staff of 57. The filature was operating this inst. with a full complement of workers.

I am, Sir,

Sir,

Bridge and their passes confiscated. No disturbance

Made by D. S. I. Lee Yee Tong Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Sir:

C. D. C. 170 reports that the Dah Sing Silk Weaving Factory situated at house 42/8 Lane 464 Yulin Road went on strike since 7 a.m. 10/10/38. 33 male and 3 female operatives are effected.

The trouble was originated on 6/10/38 when the workmen demanded their half month's wage be paid to them on 7/10/38 instead of 10/10/38, so they could use the money before the Mid-Autumn Festival. The management only granted an advance of half of their wages which was due. On 7/10/38 the workmen went on strike and presented two demands to the said management, (1) Increase of wages (2) Less deduction of one roll of silk weaven by them. October 8th. and 9th. were general festival holidays, work was not resumed. The management and workmen came to an agreement at 3 p.m. 9/10/38 when the demand of increase of wage was set aside and the management granted less deduction by one yard per roll of silk.

（批：Keep for ref. D.S.I.）
（签名：S.D.1/e. D.D.O. (D) D.C. (S/B)）

At 6 a.m. 10/10/38 all the workmen returned to their work without any trouble. At 7 a.m. same morning, a number of workmen from the new factory situated at 23 Haichow Road (under the same management) came and requested the workers to have a sympathetic strike with them. As they went on strike at 6 a.m. 10/10/38 because they still had some differences with the management with regard to the treatment. All workmen in the Dah Sing Silk Weaving Factory complied with their request and left their factory quietly at 7 a.m.

Chang Yu Tao (章在陶), the proprietor of the factory, was interviewed by detectives and he stated that he experienced no trouble with the workmen in his old factory at Lane 464/46 Yulin Road. Apparently they will return to their work as soon as the trouble is settled in the new factory, **〔此处转录不清〕**.

（批注：S / D / 1.R. 12/10 Loh.）

纠纷起源于1938年10月6日，当时工人要求将半月工资于1938年10月7日而非10月10日支付给他们，以便他们在中秋节前使用这笔钱。管理层仅同意预付到期工资的一半。1938年10月7日，工人罢工并向上述管理层提出两项要求，(1) 增加工资 (2) 减少对他们织造的每匹丝绸的扣减量。10月8日和9日为普遍节日假期，未复工。管理层与工人于1938年10月9日下午3点达成协议，此时增加工资的要求被搁置，管理层同意每匹丝绸少扣减一码。

1938年10月10日上午6时，所有工人毫无麻烦地返回工作岗位。同日早上7时，来自海州路23号新工厂（同一管理层旗下）的一些工人前来，请求工人们举行同情性罢工以支持他们。因为他们于1938年10月10日上午6时罢工，原因是他们在待遇方面与管理层仍存在一些分歧。大新丝织厂的所有工人都响应了他们的请求，并于上午7时安静地离开工厂。

The factory in question employs a complement of 300 workers including 150 males and 150 females. At 6.30 a.m. on 15/2/37, the day shift workers about 150 in number turned up to work after the Chinese New Year holiday. They carried on working until 8 a.m. 15/2/37, when the 150 day shift workers suddenly stopped work, left the factory to declare a strike.

At about 4 p.m. 15/2/37, 13 representatives including Ong Yuh Yah (王月法) and twelve others interviewed the manager Tien Zue Pao (钱序葆) and submitted a petition with the following demands.

1. The standard measurement for each roll of silk be 45 feet instead of 43 feet.
2. 30% increase of wages.
3. 30 cents boarding and lodging allowance to be paid to each employee when the weaving machines are under repairs.
4. Working hour not to exceed 10½ hours.
5. Two days' holiday in a month and wages are to be paid as usual.
6. Wages for coolies are to be increased twice a year.
7. 10 cents allowance to be paid to each worker on night shift.

（左侧批注：J.B 19/2 INTELLIGENCE REPORT）
